newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt to seek growth, price stability - Gov-Gen.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt to seek growth, price stability - Gov-Gen.

text.p: New Zealand Governor-General Sir Michael Hardie Boys said on Friday the new government would pursue sound and orthodox economic policies with a commitment to strong growth and price stability.

"That includes commitments to strong growth, to price stability, to an open, internationally-competitive economy, to prudent, conservative fiscal management with reducing taxes and debt, and to better national savings performance," Hardie Boys said in his speech at the opening of the new parliament.
The Governor-General is the representative of Queen Elizabeth, New Zealand's head of state, and his speech is written by the prime minister.
He said the policies of the new centre-right National-New Zealand First government would focus on health, education and training for Maori and settlement of outstanding Maori claims and grievances.
It would allocate more resources to education, health and social services, and law and order.

"The coalition government recognises the need to help those who are through misfortune over-represented in the statistics of dependency, educational failure, ill health, child mortality and law-breaking," he said.
The new government was working on a comprehensive programme and would introduce bills to implement its policies in the new year, Hardie Boys added.

New Zealand First, which held the balance of power, ended two months of uncertainty since the October 12 election by announcing it would form a coalition with National earlier this week. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
